  have hBouter : IsOuterDiskMultiplier B := hGn.mul F.denominator_outer

      norm_div, norm_div] at hz

      (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr hGd)).mp hz

    outerDiskMultiplier_unique_up_to_unimodular A B hcrossMod hAouter hBouter

    diskMultiplierLineBoundary_mul_ae G.numerator F.denominator,
    F.denominator_ne_zero_ae, G.denominator_ne_zero_ae]

[FALSE] A split complete order quotient with a ucp section always extends to a quotient of $C^*$-envelopes.

Take $K=[-1,1]^2$, $L=\{0\}\times[-1,1]$, $S=A(K)$, and $T=A(L)$. Restriction $q:S\to T$ is a split complete order quotient; ucp section extends an affine function of $y$ constantly in $x$. Nevertheless,

# Heat flow is not modular flow

Tomita modular time acts by algebra automorphisms.  The de Bruijn--Newman deformation is a heat
flow and already fails multiplicativity on the quadratic polynomial sector at every nonzero time.
Thus Born inverse temperature, modular time, and heat time cannot literally be one clock.

open Polynomial

/-- The exact heat operator `exp(t * D²)` on the polynomial sector of degree at most two.  On that
sector the exponential truncates after its linear term. -/
def quadraticPolynomialHeat (t : ℂ) (P : Polynomial ℂ) : Polynomial ℂ :=
  P + C t * derivative (derivative P)

@[simp]
theorem quadraticPolynomialHeat_X (t : ℂ) : quadraticPolynomialHeat t X = X := by
  simp [quadraticPolynomialHeat]

@[simp]
theorem quadraticPolynomialHeat_X_sq (t : ℂ) :
    quadraticPolynomialHeat t (X ^ 2) = X ^ 2 + C t * 2 := by
  simp [quadraticPolynomialHeat]
  norm_num

/-- **Heat/modular no-go.** At nonzero time the quadratic heat operator is not multiplicative,
whereas every modular automorphism is.  The failure is the carré-du-champ cross term `2t`. -/
theorem quadraticPolynomialHeat_not_multiplicative {t : ℂ} (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    quadraticPolynomialHeat t (X * X) ≠
      quadraticPolynomialHeat t X * quadraticPolynomialHeat t X := by
  rw [show X * X = X ^ 2 by ring, quadraticPolynomialHeat_X_sq,
    quadraticPolynomialHeat_X]
  intro h
  have hcoeff := congrArg (fun P : Polynomial ℂ => P.coeff 0) h
  simp at hcoeff
  exact ht hcoeff

/-- If the quadratic heat operator is multiplicative even on the single test `X * X`, its time is
zero.  This is the positive rigidity statement left by the no-go. -/
theorem quadraticPolynomialHeat_mul_X_eq_iff (t : ℂ) :
    quadraticPolynomialHeat t (X * X) =
      quadraticPolynomialHeat t X * quadraticPolynomialHeat t X ↔ t = 0 := by
  constructor
  · contrapose!
    exact quadraticPolynomialHeat_not_multiplicative
  · rintro rfl
    simp [quadraticPolynomialHeat]

end
end RHTower

Transporting the free wedge modular conjugation by the incoming Møller operator gives the
incoming conjugation `J_in = V_in J₀ V_in⁻¹`; the interacting conjugation is
`J = V_in J₀ V_out⁻¹` and the physical scattering operator is `S = V_in V_out⁻¹`.  From the single
fact that `J₀` is an involution one gets

```text
S = J_in ∘ J,        J = J_in ∘ S,
```

so the whole scattering law is the relative position of two conjugations.  Complex conjugate
linearity of `J₀` makes both conjugations antiunitary and their composite complex linear: the
relative modular operator is a genuine unitary.  When the interacting conjugation is itself an
involution, the relative unitary satisfies the reality law `J_in M J_in = M⁻¹`.

The factorizing `n`-particle multiplier is the product of the two-particle function over all
rapidity pairs.  It depends only on rapidity differences — so it is invariant under the common
boost — and on a two-particle chamber it is literally the input two-particle function.

section Linearity

variable {A B C : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace ℂ A]
  [NormedAddCommGroup B] [NormedSpace ℂ B]

/-- Complex linearity of a real-linear map: the unitary half of the modular dictionary. -/
def IsComplexLinearMap (f : A → B) : Prop := ∀ (c : ℂ) (x : A), f (c • x) = c • f x

/-- Complex conjugate linearity: the antiunitary half. -/
def IsConjugateLinearMap (f : A → B) : Prop :=
  ∀ (c : ℂ) (x : A), f (c • x) = conj c • f x

/-- **Two antiunitaries compose to a unitary.** -/
theorem IsConjugateLinearMap.comp {g : B → C} {f : A → B}
    (hg : IsConjugateLinearMap g) (hf : IsConjugateLinearMap f) :
    IsComplexLinearMap (g ∘ f) := by
  intro c x
  show g (f (c • x)) = c • g (f x)
  rw [hf, hg]
  simp

theorem IsComplexLinearMap.comp_conjugate {g : B → C} {f : A → B}
    (hg : IsComplexLinearMap g) (hf : IsConjugateLinearMap f) :
    IsConjugateLinearMap (g ∘ f) := by
  intro c x
  show g (f (c • x)) = conj c • g (f x)
  rw [hf, hg]

theorem IsConjugateLinearMap.comp_complex {g : B → C} {f : A → B}
    (hg : IsConjugateLinearMap g) (hf : IsComplexLinearMap f) :
    IsConjugateLinearMap (g ∘ f) := by
  intro c x
  show g (f (c • x)) = conj c • g (f x)
  rw [hf, hg]

/-- The inverse of a complex-linear isometric equivalence is complex linear. -/
theorem isComplexLinearMap_symm (V : A ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] B) (hV : IsComplexLinearMap V) :
    IsComplexLinearMap V.symm := by
  intro c y
  apply V.injective
  rw [V.apply_symm_apply, hV, V.apply_symm_apply]
